Config: G+9+R · 10 storeys + roof  |  Grid: 10×14 lines · footprint 45'-1" × 46'-7"
Sync Floors
Draw columns, beams & slabs once on this floor, then copy that layout to any other floors. Linked floors update automatically whenever you edit the source floor — check "Edit independently" on a floor any time to break the link and customize it.
Multi-Floor Draw
Turn this on and pick floors below — anything you draw from now on (column, beam, slab, wall, stair, lift, etc.) will be placed on the active floor AND copied onto every floor you check here. These are independent copies, not live-linked (use "Sync Floors" for live-linked copies).
Staircase Setup
Pick the stair type, landings, flights and sizes, then click a column.
Lift Setup
Set the lift shaft's clear size and which side its door opens on, then click "Set — Now Click a Column". The lift shaft is auto-placed on the left side of the column you click.
Roof-top Item Setup
Pick what this is, then draw its footprint by clicking two corners anywhere you like (usually on the Roof story, but you can place it on any floor).
You'll place this exactly where you want — draw it like the Beam tool (click one corner, then the opposite corner).
Drawing Sheets
Generate a printable plan sheet (with title block) from the current canvas view, or an auto-dimensioned plan/section drawn from project data.
Dimensioned Construction Drawings (auto-generated)
The four buttons above print ONE member type per sheet (with its own schedule table) instead of everything together — other member types still show as faint outlines for spatial context, but only the sheet's own type gets full label/size/load annotation. Drawn fresh from your grid lines, column positions, and story heights (not a screenshot) — bay-by-bay and overall dimension strings, grid bubbles, real column sizes, and story-height dimensions. This is a dimension-reference sheet, not a fully drafted architectural/structural drawing set (no walls, openings, reinforcement detail, or foundation depth) — see the note on each sheet for exactly what's shown.
Canvas Snapshot Sheet
Opens the current story's plan (a snapshot of whatever the canvas is currently showing, including any manual dimensions/text you've placed) in a new tab with a title block, ready to print or "Save as PDF". Zoom/pan the canvas first to frame what you want. If the print dialog doesn't work for you (some embedded/sandboxed browsers block it), use Download Plan Image (PNG) instead — a direct file download, no print dialog involved.
DXF export writes real AutoCAD-readable entities (Column/BEAM/ST.SLAB LAYOUT/R.C.C WALL/GRID LINE/text — the same layer names used by imported reference drawings) for the current story, including grid lines and member-mark/size labels. "Foundation Layout" instead writes PILE/PILE_CAP circles+outlines, grid, labels, and a text schedule from the lowest story's columns. "Combined" writes all four (Foundation/Column/Beam/Slab) as separate side-by-side sheets in one file, each with its own schedule table. A true DWG (binary) export is not available; DWG is a closed Autodesk format with no public spec to write to from a browser app.
BIM Export
Writes an IFC4 (.ifc) STEP file — Project → Site → Building → Storeys, with every Column/Beam/Wall/Slab across all stories as a real extruded solid, openable in Revit, ArchiCAD, Navisworks, Solibri, BIMvision, etc. Scope: structural framing only (cores/stairs/lifts, openings and 2D annotation are not included); element GUIDs are randomly generated tokens, not tied to a persistent project ID, so re-exporting creates new GUIDs each time.
Schematic Elevation / Section (single-axis, undimensioned)
These show story levels and column centerlines projected onto one axis — a schematic reference only, not a drafted elevation/section with beam depths, walls, openings or hidden-line removal. Use the Drawing Canvas' 3D view for an actual visual walkthrough of the model.

Add Beam Size
This size becomes the active pick for new beams you draw.
Add Grill
Window grills are placed automatically on every window on this story. Balcony grills you draw yourself, in whatever shape you like — this size applies to every segment you draw next.
Every window on the current story (0 found) gets a grill sized to that window's own height and sill — the height field above isn't used for windows.
